reviewed_version: Supplied publisher version of record, DOI 10.1007/s00222-025-01383-4; 45 PDF pages, printed 657–701; online 2025-10-23
outcome: Three confirmed Minor findings; main velocity resolvent conclusions not refuted
summary: Explicit counterexamples establish excessive all-q gradient/pressure membership in Theorem 9.5, a false arbitrary-graph fixed-ball Poincare assertion in Remark 2.3, and missing boundary-flux compatibility in Theorem A.1. Concrete local corrections and a finite-q completion of exterior uniqueness are supplied. Independent acceptance of this bounded review is complete; the substantive scientific decision remains pending and human_reviews is empty.

findings.claim: For any bounded planar Lipschitz domain and 1<q<infinity, all solenoidal Lq forcing yields a W0^{1,q} velocity and Lq pressure.
findings.evidence: Report Section 2 gives an exact reentrant-sector construction at lambda=1. nu in (1/2,3/5) solves sin(3pi nu/2)=nu; the displayed clamped biharmonic stream function has velocity r^nu and gradient/pressure r^{nu-1}. A smooth away-vertex boundary collar correction makes the force stream function zero on the whole boundary while retaining bounded forcing. Thus F is bounded and belongs to L5_sigma, u lies in H10 and Linfinity, p in L2, but neither gradient u nor p is L5. Mean subtraction does not remove the singularity. Energy uniqueness excludes the claimed stronger solution.
proof_checks: Angular value and derivative vanish at both walls; Phi''(0)=-4nu cos(omega nu) is nonzero.
Pressure is the correctly signed harmonic conjugate giving grad p=J grad Delta psi.
Cutoff supported inside exact sector neighborhood; rounded outer geometry is smooth away from the sole corner.
Boundary collar has zero value/normal derivative and prescribed Laplacian b.
Force stream function in W0^{1,5}, so compactly supported scalar approximation yields L5_sigma membership even under closure definition.
Divergent integral exponent 5(nu-1)+1<-1; positive nu gives energy integrability.
All domain, lambda, pressure normalization, and force assumptions satisfied.
findings.consequence: The all-q regularity membership is false. Velocity estimate (9.13), Theorem 9.4 and main Theorem 1.1 are not contradicted.
findings.repair: Separate velocity resolvent estimates from gradient/pressure membership; restrict the latter to the domain-dependent interval near 2 or strengthen boundary regularity.
findings.classification_basis: Secondary regularity overstatement with bounded effect; not a demonstrated failure of the paper's main velocity theorem.

findings.claim: The fixed-ball trace Poincare estimate with beta average over D_{2R} holds for every Lipschitz graph.
findings.evidence: R=1,d=2, psi(x)=max(0,3-12|x-1/2|). D2 misses the entire vertical transition strip 0.45<x<0.55. eta=chi(x)zeta(x,y), with chi 0 left and1 right and zeta1 near B2, has gradient zero on D2, beta strictly between0and1, and positive Lq' trace oscillation on I1. Both components and both trace patches have positive measure.
findings.consequence: The arbitrary-slope assertion is false; this graph violates Theorem2.2's small-slope condition.
findings.repair: Take one average over a connected graph box P_R={|x'|<4R, psi(x')<xd<(4M+4)R}; trace/Poincare with constants C(M) and global dual-test gradient norm preserve all localization powers. No additional u/F support is needed.
findings.classification_basis: Explicit geometric local repair suffices for the main planar use; no resolvent counterexample.

findings.claim: Arbitrary W^{1,q} boundary data admit a divergence-free Stokes solution.
findings.evidence: Unit disk, q=2, f(x)=x: all printed hypotheses hold, but integral_boundary f dot n=2pi, contradicting divergence-free solvability.
findings.consequence: Appendix A's actual f=-w has div w=0, so its compatibility is already satisfied.
findings.classification_basis: Necessary omitted hypothesis in auxiliary theorem with immediate repair; checked applications unaffected.

checks.source_locations: Publisher PDF pp.38-40 / printed694-696, Theorems9.4 and9.5
checks.reason: The source actually asserts W_0^(1,q) velocity and L^q pressure for every 1<q<infinity in an arbitrary bounded planar Lipschitz domain, although its interpolation proof controls velocity only. Root independently checked the sector construction: omega=3pi/2 has a root nu in(1/2,3/5) of sin(omega nu)=nu; the four angular boundary values of Phi and Phi' vanish, Phi is nonzero, and the stated pressure has gradient J grad Delta psi_s. A smooth collar correction v=d^2 b(s)/2 away from the corner imposes Delta v=b while preserving clamped data. The resulting force is J grad(h-Delta psi+psi), bounded, with zero-boundary stream function in W_0^(1,5), hence genuinely in L_sigma^5. Near the vertex u is bounded and in H_0^1, p is in L2, whereas nonzero angular pieces of grad u and p have radial power r^(nu-1) and fail L5 since5nu-4<-1. Energy uniqueness at lambda=1 excludes another claimed strong solution.

checks.source_locations: Theorem9.4 and main-claim description; full report
checks.reason: This refutes the extra all-q existence class, not the bounded-velocity estimate. The preceding main planar proof only needs a permitted q>2 close to2. Limiting gradient/pressure regularity to an admissible boundary-dependent interval, or strengthening boundary regularity, removes the demonstrated overstatement without asserting a new universal regularity theorem. Minor follows the verified scope of impact.

The image explicitly removes a small-slope restriction. For psi(x)=max(0,3-12|x-1/2|), the strip0.45<x<0.55 lies above B2 because psi>=2.4. Thus D2 has positive-area portions on both sides. A compactly supported smooth eta changing from0 to1 only in that empty strip has grad eta=0 in D2; its D2 average is strictly between0 and1 and both constant trace values occur on positive-length pieces of I1. The printed trace-Poincare inequality therefore fails. Replacing the averaging set by the connected graph box |x'|<4R, psi(x')<x_d<(4M+4)R, using one common average and the already available global test-gradient norm, is compatible with the localization supports and cancellation integral g=0. This is a local fixed-domain failure, not failure of the main estimate.

checks.source_locations: Publisher PDF pp.39-40, TheoremA.1 and its displayed application
checks.reason: For the unit disk, q=2 and boundary f(x)=x, all printed smoothness and connected-boundary hypotheses hold but total normal flux is2pi. A divergence-free extension is impossible by the divergence theorem. The omitted zero-flux assumption is necessary. The actual application has f=-w with div w=0 and already satisfies it; adding that hypothesis repairs this obstruction without purporting to re-prove all cited external regularity results.
